_comment: Narrative / myth types for narrative-engineering deliberations. The selected type's prompt_fragment is injected into every agent turn as the NARRATIVE TARGET (and into the Planner's brief), so the whole panel engineers the same kind of story. Users may also type a custom description instead of choosing a preset. Add a type by adding one object -- no R changes.

narrative_types.name: Origin myth
narrative_types.description: Explains how something came to be; grounds identity and meaning.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer an ORIGIN MYTH: a story that explains how the thing at issue came to be, grounding identity and shared meaning. It should answer 'why are things this way?' with narrative causes -- ancestors, first acts, primordial choices -- not analysis.

narrative_types.name: Hero's journey
narrative_types.description: A transformation arc: call, ordeal, return with a gift.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a HERO'S JOURNEY: a protagonist is called out of the ordinary, faces ordeals that transform them, and returns bearing a gift the community needs. The transformation must be earned through loss or sacrifice, not granted.

narrative_types.name: Parable
narrative_types.description: A compact story carrying a transferable moral.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a PARABLE: a short, concrete story whose events carry a transferable moral without stating it as doctrine. Everyday characters, one pivotal choice, an ending that lands the lesson through consequence rather than commentary.

narrative_types.name: Cautionary tale
narrative_types.description: Dramatizes a failure mode and its consequences.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a CAUTIONARY TALE: dramatize the failure mode at issue through a character who plausibly commits it, and let the consequences unfold with honest severity. The warning must emerge from the story's logic, not from moralizing.

narrative_types.name: Trickster tale
narrative_types.description: Subverts authority and assumptions through cunning; holds ambiguity.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a TRICKSTER TALE: a cunning figure subverts authority, rules, or settled assumptions, exposing what the order conceals. Preserve moral ambiguity -- the trickster should be neither hero nor villain, and the reader should be left productively unsettled.

narrative_types.name: Foundation myth
narrative_types.description: Legitimates an institution, practice, or community charter.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a FOUNDATION MYTH: a story that legitimates an institution, practice, or community -- its founding act, the price paid for it, and the obligation it lays on those who inherit it. Beware: this type is the most exposed to propaganda misuse; the Red Team should press hard.

narrative_types.name: Renewal myth
narrative_types.description: Collapse and rebirth; hope on the far side of loss.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a RENEWAL MYTH: an order collapses -- through its own flaw, catastrophe, or exhaustion -- and something genuinely new is reborn from what survives. The hope must be paid for; renewal that costs nothing persuades no one.

narrative_types.name: Fable
narrative_types.description: Non-human actors; a pointed, memorable lesson.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a FABLE: non-human actors -- animals, objects, forces -- enact a pointed lesson in a brief, memorable arc. The displacement into non-human characters should let the audience see their own behaviour without feeling accused.

narrative_types.name: Zen koan
narrative_types.description: A brief paradoxical exchange that defeats analysis and provokes insight.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a ZEN KOAN: a brief, concrete exchange or question about the matter at hand that cannot be resolved by discursive reasoning -- the impasse itself is the teaching. No explanation, no stated moral, no resolution; end on the turning point. A koan that can be answered analytically has failed.

narrative_types.name: Haiku
narrative_types.description: A cycle of short image-poems; one concrete moment each, meaning by juxtaposition.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a HAIKU CYCLE: a small sequence of three-line poems, each capturing ONE concrete sensory moment that embodies the matter at hand -- an image from nature or daily life, a seasonal anchor, and a cut (juxtaposition) that lets meaning arise unstated. No abstraction, no commentary, no moralizing; if a line explains, replace it with an image.

narrative_types.name: Taoist style
narrative_types.description: A parable in the manner of Zhuangzi/Laozi: reversal, wu wei, the useful uselessness.
narrative_types.prompt_fragment: Engineer a TAOIST-STYLE PARABLE in the manner of Zhuangzi or the Laozi: a short story or saying built on reversal -- the soft outlasting the hard, the useless tree left standing, the sage who leads by yielding (wu wei). Hold the paradox gently rather than resolving it, favour water, valley and uncarved-wood imagery over argument, and state no doctrine: the reader should arrive at the point the text never announces.
